questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Future exchange students should know that living off campus offers more independence but requires careful planning. Be prepared for higher costs, longer commutes, and make sure to check the lease terms. Also, get familiar with the local public transport system and neighborhoods.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I would advise future exchange students to start the registration process early, as it can be time-consuming. Make sure to double-check all deadlines and requirements. Don’t hesitate to reach out to contacts for clarification, and keep track of all documents and approvals.

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of courses at my host institution was quite diverse. There were courses available for beginners as well as more advanced ones, catering to different levels of academic backgrounds. Some courses were challenging, requiring a strong foundation in the subject, while others were more introductory and accessible. It's important to choose courses that align with your knowledge and academic goals, and don't hesitate to ask for recommendations from professors or fellow students.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: In general, the style was a bit more hands-on and interactive compared to the more lecture-based format at UCPH.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I highly recommend exploring both the local area and nearby cities during weekends or holidays. Take time to visit local landmarks, museums, and parks—it's a great way to experience the culture. If possible, go on day trips to nearby cities or scenic spots. In Italy, for example, places like Lake Como, Cinque Terre, or Florence are all beautiful and easily reachable. Also, try to attend local festivals, markets, or concerts for a more authentic experience. And don't forget to enjoy the local food scene—whether it’s a casual café or a fine dining experience!

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Adjusting to the local culture at my exchange site was relatively easy, but it took some time to fully get comfortable. People were generally welcoming, and there were plenty of opportunities to learn about the local customs and traditions through social events and interactions with locals. The language barrier was a bit of a challenge at first, but many people spoke English, which made things easier. Immersing myself in local activities, trying the food, and getting involved in university events really helped me adapt. It was a gradual process, but overall, it was an enjoyable experience.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Look out for university parties, local festivals, or casual meetups—these are often relaxed environments where people are open to chatting and making new friends.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: One of the cultural differences I found challenging was the pace of life. In some places, things move much more slowly, especially when it comes to service in restaurants or waiting in line. It was a bit of an adjustment compared to the faster pace I was used to.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I really appreciated the strong sense of community and the importance placed on socializing in the culture. People often make time for meals with family or friends, which created a warm and welcoming atmosphere. I also loved the emphasis on food and tradition; every meal felt like an experience, and it was great to try so many local dishes. The relaxed attitude toward life, with a focus on enjoying the moment, was something I truly admired as well. Additionally, the deep appreciation for art, history, and local customs made exploring the area rich and fulfilling.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Start the registration process early, embrace the local culture and be flexible and patient

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Costs can add up quickly, especially in larger cities. Plan ahead and try to set a monthly budget for things like food, transportation, and leisure activities. Local markets and cooking your own meals can help save money.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange experience was the opportunity to immerse myself in a new culture and gain a deeper understanding of the world. I really enjoyed meeting people from diverse backgrounds, learning about their perspectives. Academically, it was rewarding to experience a different approach to teaching and learning, which broadened my academic horizons.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge during my exchange was adjusting to the differences in academic systems. The approach to assignments, exams, and even the overall structure of the courses was quite different from what I was used to.
